items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: well, I guess he just offered me the chair in the orchestra.

ctx.x: Do you recall the circumstances of joining that great orchestra?

No, but, gee, what . . . I don’t know how I happened to go . . . well, I guess he just offered me the chair in the orchestra. It’s interesting that Chick was not the musician that Fletcher Henderson was, but he had an uncanny feeling for good musicians, and everybody knew that, and you were really . . . oh, you were given a feeling of importance when he asked you to join his band, you know? And that’s with me, too. He had very good taste in music and in musicians, and he was some other kind of drummer, as you…
Could you contrast sort of the different musical styles of playing or the different demands on you playing in the two orchestras? Does anything come to mind that . . .

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I was with Fletcher first and then Chick's

ctx.x: I'd like to come now, you know -- we brought up your sax playing, your arranging, and your interest in the trumpet and your taking up the trumpet, which brings us to somewhere in 1928-29. Now let's go on to the band-leading and playing and other things that came up after that point. I'd like to get some notion -- is the next major thing that you do going to Fletcher Henderson's band, or is there something else that goes on before that?
Let me see ... I'm trying to remember when if I was with Chick Webb's band.
